protocol.study_type: Synthetic assumption stress study, not field validation
protocol.research_question: Does the benefit of a denser network persist when endurance, launch latency and reserve assumptions become more conservative?

random_streams.bootstrap: default_rng([1, seed]); identical season draws for both arms

protocol.primary_metric: Pooled fraction of real alerts reached within 900 seconds of alert receipt, including rejected alerts in the denominator
comparisons: Each non-reference condition minus reference within the same layout and wind: 16 paired contrasts
25 bases minus 9 bases within the same condition and wind: 10 paired contrasts
protocol.uncertainty: 95% pointwise percentile season-cluster bootstrap intervals, Monte Carlo sampling error only; not simultaneous intervals or input uncertainty bounds
non_goals: No new dispatch policy, physical model, detector evaluation or live flight integration
No empirical claim that endurance loses 25%, launch takes 180 seconds, or reserve should be 35%
No forecast-weather availability, field performance, optimization or regulatory claim
No changes to historical outputs or the 2026-11-07 anchor

interpretation: Stress values are hypothetical, not measured aircraft derating or operating advice.
All scenarios share real and false alerts; false alerts consume fleet time.
Intervals are pointwise season-cluster Monte Carlo intervals, not field uncertainty.
Wind is fixed eastward throughout each season; no weather probabilities are inferred.
Blank p90 with p90_unreachable=True denotes infinity; rejected alerts remain included.
Historical proxy costs are unchanged, not supplier quotes or stress-adjusted economics.
Launch consumes fleet busy time but not airborne endurance in the unchanged model.
Source hashes identify executed files even when Git worktree is dirty.
